LanguageData.CC_Settings_Notables_Tip: The towns within reach of the colony (the nearest few, and any it has dealt with) each have a few people the colony knows by name: the town's head (their people's own leader at their seat, else a headman, reeve, mayor or administrator by their era), a likely heir, an envoy and a known trader, made with their people's own kinds. Faces the colony met who went home join them: a prisoner set free, a wounded guest tended, a camp's leader, a guest of rank, an envoy, a visiting trader. Each regards the colony and some of its people from their people's goodwill and memory, their own nature, and what passed between them, and remembers it. They age, can die, and are followed in their role. A town's card on the region map shows them, and the region window's Peoples under Faces. Off: nobody is kept, and those kept are let go.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_Notables: The nearby towns' head, heir, envoy and trader by name, and the faces the colony met.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_NeighbourLetters_Tip: From a town's card on the region map (or the region window's Peoples under Faces) a colonist can write to one of the neighbours: greetings, condolences for a loss the colony knows of, a warning of a threat to them, asking for news, an invitation to visit, or asking for a little help. They sit down at a table to write it (a tribe gives a spoken message instead) and it waits in the mailbag at the gate until someone going their way takes it (the post rider, traders, visitors, a camp breaking up, the colony's own caravan, or your own rider if you send one); the answer comes back the same way, with gifts when it brings some by their messenger. With the post off in the settings, a messenger of their people comes to the gate for each letter, as before. With a powered comms console and a people with the means to answer, a call does the same at once, or an aide takes a message and they call back later; what a call sends still comes by courier. How it is taken follows their nature, how they regard the colony and the writer, and the writer's way with words. One letter at a time to each; with the post, twelve open at most (without it, three).
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_NeighbourLetters: Write to the neighbours by hand, or call them on a comms console.
